topics.topic: Action for correcting customer kind and fiscal data
questions: Which action changes a customer's kind, tax id or legal name after the Customer has been recorded?
Which action lets the owner add, change or clear a Customer's tax id and legal name after recording it?
Can the owner correct a customer's kind, tax id and legal name, and if so is that done by `correct a customer` with the same revision and restriction rules?

quotes:
Registry is the one home of a customer's personal data: no other service keeps
a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it
issued (R0-80).
| correct a customer | owner | the Customer with the new contact data, next revision | unknown customer refused; an erased customer cannot be corrected; a stale revision refused (R0-35) |

A customer's living personal data — name, contact data, tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF),
legal name — and the object's address are held only by Registry.
judgement.divergence: One implementer lets `correct a customer` change or clear kind, tax id and legal name under the Customer revision rules; another treats those fields as immutable after recording, which the owner and services needing corrected billing data notice.
judgement.why: Registry promises to own the fields but carries no action that promises their correction after recording.

topics.topic: Actor, trust boundary, and temporary status of the legacy VPS Registry during migration
questions: What actor and trust boundary describes the legacy VPS Registry during export and migration, before it is retired?
What is the status and trust boundary of the legacy VPS Registry while it holds the personal data used by the migration?

What actor and trust-boundary category does the legacy VPS Registry and its migration export belong to, and is it an explicit temporary exception to the rule that every non-production instance holds no production personal data?

quotes:
- **Test instances** — any other instance (the agent's machine, a rig, a
  developer laptop). Each holds its own identity space and no production
  personal data; nothing moves between an instance and production except by an
  explicit import (R0-34).

The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once. The owner picks the
projects: today "Comunidad de Propietarios C/ del Progreso 140"
(`37241411-f235-4a32-bb31-9629d1079dd2`) and the project of Uliana Kolpacheva
(`c276a851-9b8a-44c7-bbf7-20e363b0ad5f`), under the ids Client Portal already
names.

| import projects with their identity | owner, confirming, from the VPS instance: the projects the owner picks (R0-79) | those projects under the identities they carry, with their customers, objects, rooms and pointers (ids kept), links intact (R0-34, R0-44, R0-50); a v1 `customer_ref` that is not a Registry-minted id becomes a new Customer with a minted `customer_ref`, the old value moving to its tax id when it is one (R0-80) | any conflict with an id production holds refuses the whole import, nothing applied, and the owner may retry after correcting it; after the first successful import the operation is closed and refused (R0-79) |
judgement.why: The legacy VPS Registry is a non-production instance under the stated exhaustive definition, yet it is also the source of customer and object data imported into production.

topics.topic: Conditions for retained artifact pointers and identifiers to be considered anonymised
questions: Before anonymisation, must Registry remove or reject pointers containing identifying values, must the owner attest that they are clean, or is the no-personal-value claim limited to fields Registry classifies as `personal_data`?
What must be established or changed before a project retaining its id and artifact pointers may be reported as anonymised with no personal value?
How can anonymisation guarantee that the retained project holds no personal value or permits no re-identification when its uninspected artifact pointers remain?

judgement.why: This is the same question previously judged about the conditions under which retained anonymised-project identifiers and pointers are non-identifying.

precedent.topic: Conditions ensuring retained anonymised-project identifiers and pointers are non-identifying
quotes: A project's technical identity, status and artifact pointers are kept only where it is shown that they no longer allow re-identification and a justified purpose for keeping them is recorded; `validate` then answers `archived`. Otherwise the record is deleted whole, and `validate` answers `not_found`.
Narrowed by R0-60: the owner chooses between the two when erasing; the showing and the purpose are recorded in the governance.
precedent.why: Retention is permitted only after a governance-recorded showing that the retained identity and pointers no longer allow re-identification; otherwise the project is deleted whole.

topics.topic: Meaning, concurrency role, and mutation rules of the agent-session access version
questions: Is the access version an optimistic-concurrency precondition for every mutation of a session's grants, active project and pending request?
What is the observable meaning of the access version, when does it change, and does it provide stale-write protection for owner and Kernel actions?
What state does the access version version, and exactly which accepted actions change it?

judgement.why: This is the same question previously judged about the scope, increments and concurrency use of the session access version.

precedent.topic: Scope, increments, and concurrency use of the session access version
quotes: the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.
precedent.why: Mutation preconditions, version-transition rules and stale-input behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Permitted downstream copies and exceptions to Registry as the sole living store of personal data
questions: Must later states treat Registry as the sole living store of tax id and legal name, with PresuPro retaining them only inside issued documents?
Which Registry values, if any, may Client Portal persist in its offline projection, and how is that exception reconciled with the one-home rule?
Are identifying characteristics subject to the same sole-living-copy and issued-document exception as the address?
May Client Portal persist an offline copy of Registry-held personal values, and if so, which fields and under what exception to R0-80?
May Client Portal, Cabinet or PresuPro retain snapshots containing living customer or object personal data, and if so, which values and under what explicit exception to R0-80?

quotes:
Registry is the one home of a customer's personal data: no other service keeps
a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it
issued (R0-80).

When home is
unreachable, Portal serves the last projection it was permitted to keep
locally: Portal's own snapshot of what its contract allowed (V1-2), never an
answer of Registry, and Portal changes nothing in Registry meanwhile.

| read a project context | owner; a trusted service whose token allows `personal_data` (R0-43) | the snapshot a consumer keeps: id, display name, status, address, `customer_ref` (never contact data), created and updated times (R0-04) | unknown id refused; an anonymised project answers that it was erased (R0-62); a caller whose token does not allow `personal_data` refused |

The customer's contact data and
the object's address and identifying characteristics are `personal_data`; a
project's id is not anonymous by itself and is never `open` merely for being
an id.

Client
Portal's offline projection (R0-39) holds no tax id.
judgement.why: The one-home rule forbids another service from keeping living personal-value copies, while the Portal is explicitly allowed to keep a local context projection that may contain the personal-data address, with only tax id expressly excluded.

topics.topic: Revision requirements and behavior for mutations and idempotent no-ops
questions: Do all of these actions require the current record revision and return the next revision, including actions described as idempotent when the target state already holds?
Exactly which actions must supply an expected revision, which entity's revision do they move, and do successful idempotent no-ops move it?
Which owner-interface changes must carry which revision or version, and what concurrency check applies to changes whose target has no declared revision?

judgement.why: This is the same question previously judged about revision requirements, advancement and stale-write behavior across mutations.

precedent.topic: Revision and access-version requirements, advancement, and stale-write behavior
quotes:
Every change carries CSRF protection and
is validated on the server; a change made against an older revision is refused
(R0-35).

A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change
moves. A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an
older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.

Narrowed by R0-45: the object has no revision of its own; a change of it moves
the project's.
the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
precedent.why: Mapping expected versions to mutations, defining version advancement and specifying stale or idempotent behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Actions and outcomes that require audit entries
questions: Exactly which Primary actions and outcomes create audit entries?

Which primary actions are audit-significant, specifically including room and artifact changes, session registration, pending requests and answers, active-project changes, relationship end/resume, imports, failed confirmations and audit-log erasure?

judgement.why: This is the same question previously judged about which actions and successful or refused outcomes the audit log covers.

precedent.topic: Actions and successful or refused outcomes covered by the audit log
quotes:
Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and
customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects,
restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations. Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows
are not recorded in Registry; security events of the infrastructure are
handled by the infrastructure, outside Registry.

- **Audit.** A minimal log of significant changes of state (R0-58): time, the
  acting principal (owner, which service, agent through Kernel), the change,
  the project or customer, the outcome, the contract and release version, and
  a confirmation id where the owner confirmed.
precedent.why: The exact event-selection and outcome-recording criteria are operational rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Customer fields removed or retained after erasure
questions: When a Customer is erased, are kind, tax id and legal name erased too, or do any of them survive?
When customer data is erased, are tax id and legal name erased too, or do they remain on the record?

quotes:
Erasing a customer's contact data (R0-06) is the end of its record: the
Customer keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased, and projects keep
naming it. There is no action that deletes a Customer whole.
judgement.why: Because the erased Customer keeps only its identity and erased fact, kind, tax id and legal name do not survive.
